_comment: The week tag list's cap and ordering, shared by week_tags in
The two are separate implementations in separate languages and CAPTIONS.txt
is the deliverable, so a rule applied on one side only produces a file that
reads as complete either way. That is how #221 and #222 were both found.
1. Instagram tags at most max_tags_per_post accounts on one post. Past
that the extra handles are simply not tagged when the list is pasted
in, and nothing said which ones fell off.
2. Handles that appear in a photo's own tags come before handles that
only appear as a day-level tag. The people actually in the pictures
are the ones worth the slots, so they survive the cut by construction.
3. Within each of those two groups the original traversal order holds, so
the list is stable rather than dictionary order.
4. Handles are deduplicated case-insensitively, since Instagram handles
are not case sensitive and tagging both spellings tags one person
_provenance: 20 tags and 5 collaborators per post, confirmed by Dan on 2026-08-10. Instagram has changed limits of this kind before, so the number lives in code with this date rather than typed inline at each use.

cases._what: under the cap: everything survives, photo tags still lead
a handle tagged on a photo outranks one only tagged on the day
photo order decides the order within the photo group
one handle spelled three ways is one person
exactly at the cap, nothing is dropped
one past the cap: the last day-level handle is the one that goes
over the cap, somebody in a photo keeps their slot and a day-level handle loses one
the whole week counts as one list, not one per day
